stem: Determine between which two consecutive integers the following irrational number lies, without using a calculator. Give the smaller integer first. $\sqrt[3]{{=N}}$
solution: Find the perfect cubes on either side of ${=N}$: ${=n}^{3} = {=n ** 3}$ and ${=n + 1}^{3} = {=(n + 1) ** 3}$.
notes: Same skeleton as the book's ex1-11-20e to h, with larger radicands (the book stops at cube root 30; here the lower integer n runs 4 to 9, so the radicand runs 65 to 999 and the cubes needed are 64 up to 1000). Radicand = n^3 + r with 1 <= r <= 3n^2 + 3n, i.e. strictly between consecutive cubes, so never a perfect cube. Cubes up to 10^3 are the ceiling, matching what a Grade 10 learner is expected to know without a calculator. Kept as a separate family from the square-root one so the radical sign is always printed the book's way (no explicit index 2).
